  • 5. The Four-Gate Verdict Machine [Part 2/6]: Subtopics: Counterevidence is submission-complete; Transitive closure is a path proof, not a slogan; Partition verification is global across the admitted submission; Consensus identity removes narrative, not responsibility — Each act ends in one consequence class: A malformed whole submission is inadmissible. A recognized submission reports decision: partition, review, relation, or none; it does not acquire a blanket database-execution verdict. — Spec/Table: 1. Syntax and stage isolation; What the recognizer establishes: Strict JSON, exact keys, closed symbols, authenticated actor, unique IDs, bounded sizes, one act family, matching artifactHash; What it refuses to let the proposal do: Smuggle duplicate fields, foreign opcodes, mixed stages, self-declared actors, or unbounded matter | ****2. — Key Rules/Claims: operative — a recognized act with a consensus identity. | lawful_non_operative — a valid review request, which creates no operative identity claim. | anti_knowledge — a valid rejection of other matter. | typed_fault — preserved residue with a fault code and no standing.

  • 8. From Duplicate Records to Evidence-Linked Relationship Graphs [Part 4/6]: The commercial value is not “AI deduplication” as a slogan. It is a defensible identity substrate on which relationship paths can be inspected. A six-hop query can be a useful exploration horizon. It is not proof of influence, consent, or authority.
  • 9. The 2026 Research Landscape: Proposal Quality Is Not Transition Standing [Part 5/6]: The current research supports a hybrid division of labor: models can improve nomination, comparison, and review, while deterministic systems must decide which declared predicates actually hold. The sources do not endorse AINA, and their results need their original scopes. — Spec/Table: Teofili et al., Can we trust LLM Self-Explanations for Entity Resolution?, June 2026 preprint; What it establishes: Across three LLMs, ten datasets, and multiple prompting strategies, self-explanations were often unstable, weakly faithful, and poorly aligned with counterfactual evidence.
